messages:
Alex Chen: Quick heads-up — enabling FP8-quant KV on last night's build caused a decode p95 bump while cutting KV memory in half. profiling below, want opinions before i dig deeper.
Priya Nair: Numbers? short repro? :eyes:
Alex Chen: Repro and raw output i ran locally: 
```
Model: redwood-7b-quant
HW: A100 80GB
Mode: KV-int8 store + KV-fp8 decoding path
Batch: 4 (dynamic batching enabled)
Seq_len: 1024 (long tokens)
p50_decode: 0.31s -> 0.29s
p95_decode: 1.12s -> 1.30s   # ~16% regression
KV_mem_usage: 4.2GB -> 2.1GB
Notes: p50 improved slightly but tail worsened, memory halved as expected with fp8 store
```
Marco Diaz: p50 up, p95 worse -> smells like a tail fallback or extra work for some requests. Did kernel selector switch to a fallback path for some batches?
Jess Liu: Also check batching heuristics — if seq lengths vary we might be merging long+short which spikes tail.
Alex Chen: I instrumented the stack — most of the extra time is in a dequant path called dequantize_kv_fallback that runs on CPU during decode. Kernel selector chose fp8 fused kernel for attention, but KV read path is doing int8->fp32 via CPU dequant when GPU-resident KV exceeds threshold.
Priya Nair: Can you paste perf counters? bandwidth/memcopy times?
Alex Chen: Perf snippet: 
```
PERF_SNAPSHOT:
L1D_MISS_RATE: 22%
MEM_BANDWIDTH_UTIL: 58GB/s (on a 700GB/s device)
CUDA_MEMCPY_TIME: 34ms per batch (nvlink / host mem copies)
CPU_DEQUANT_TIME: 120ms per decode for some batches
BRANCH_MISPRED: low
```
Marco Diaz: 34ms memcpy per batch is huge. Looks like we spill FP8 KV to host_compressed store and then do CPU-side dequant on read. That would explain the p95 spikes when selector chooses host path.
Jess Liu: Where does calibration affect this? FP8 needs scale metadata; are we recalibrating per-block on read? that could be extra ops.
Priya Nair: Our FP8 KV stores per-tensor scale and does a cheap per-block scale adjust on read to prevent overflow. If the read path is on CPU we do scalar loops; on GPU we have a vectorized path.
Alex Chen: Repro flags I used: `KV_STORE=host_compressed KERNEL_POLICY=auto BATCHER=coalescer` — forcing policy to gpu-prefer causes kernel selector to pick fused_fp8_kv_kernel and the p95 goes back down to ~1.05s, but throughput drops under heavy memory pressure.
Marco Diaz: So root cause = kernel selection + placement decision + lack of GPU-side dequantic convert for fallback. Two levers: prefer GPU-resident KV for long seqs, or implement a fast GPU vectorized convert so CPU fallback not needed.
Jess Liu: Also adjust batching heuristic: if seq_len variance > threshold, disable coalescing for that request to avoid mixing and reduce tail.
Priya Nair: Proposed plan: (1) modify kernel selector to prefer GPU_fused when fp8_kv && seq_len>512 && gpu_mem_available>threshold; (2) add a GPU vectorized fp8->fp32 convert kernel to avoid CPU dequant; (3) emit selector telemetry when CPU fallback chosen so perf-bot can alert; (4) add CI perf test for long-seq mixed-precision decode.
Alex Chen: i prototyped the vectorized convert kernel and initial numbers look good: p95 -> 1.05s, KV mem remains ~2.1GB, p50 stays 0.29s. throughput stable in our quick loop. i'll open a PR.
perf-bot: New perf alert created: KV_FP8_CPU_FALLBACK_HIGH_LATENCY (alert_id=3291) — https://perf.internal/alerts/3291
Marco Diaz: Good. can we also log when we evict GPU KV to host_compressed? add metric kv_evict_events and kv_dequant_path{cpu|gpu}.
Jess Liu: Also add a small opt to batching: prefer low-latency path for requests flagged latency_sensitive (endpoint flag).
Priya Nair: Alex — can you open the PR and tag Marco + Jess for review and add the perf numbers in PR description? we'll run nightly perf lanes after merge.
Alex Chen: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4823 — includes vectorized GPU convert + selector patch + telemetry. assigned Marco/ Jess.
Marco Diaz: Reviewing now, left initial comments inline.
Jess Liu: Thx all. We'll monitor the perf lanes tomorrow and post results here. if regressions persist we can rollback fp8_kv default. :thumbsup:
